caption:
The AI put catch first "to handle errors early". It reads fine. Would you merge it?

Look at the card. When pay rejects, catch runs and shows "Failed". But catch also returns a new promise, and because the handler didn't throw, that promise resolves successfully. So the next then runs too. The user sees "Failed" and then "Order placed".

Order matters in a promise chain. Put the success step first and catch last, so a failure skips the success step.

With async/await it's harder to get wrong: put the success toast inside the try block, right after await pay(cart).

Source: MDN, Promise.prototype.catch().
